title: When the dollar was as good as gold

probes.question: Under the Bretton Woods system, the dollar was convertible to what for foreign governments and central banks?
True or false: on 15 August 1971 the United States ended the convertibility of the dollar to gold.

image.alt: The white, red-roofed Mount Washington Hotel at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, with autumn trees and mountains behind it.

panels.text: In July 1944, delegates met at the Mount Washington Hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, and signed an agreement on the last day.
Countries guaranteed to convert their currencies into US dollars. The US linked the dollar to gold at $35 an ounce, so foreign governments and central banks could swap dollars for gold.
The agreement also set up the International Monetary Fund to monitor exchange rates.
By 1970 the US had seen its gold coverage fall from 55% to 22%. On 15 August 1971 it ended the convertibility of the dollar to gold, which effectively brought the system to an end.
